data.description:
## Problem `v2BrowserDownloadWait` in Sources/SocketHandlers/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift (the `if let path` branch, ~line 792 onward) watches the target's parent directory with a `DispatchSource.makeFileSystemObjectSource` and treats the file as ready only when `pathIsReady()` sees `size > 0`. A file that is created empty and then written in place produces one directory event at create time (size still 0, so not ready) and no further directory event for the data write, because the directory's own vnode does not change when a child's contents change. The wait then runs to its full timeout even though the file appeared and filled. Atomic-rename writes (`mv` into place, which is what a real WKDownload does) work, which is why the C11-209 validation passed. Pre-existing, unchanged by C11-209, confirmed real by its delegator. ## Fix When the directory event fires and the file now exists but is not yet ready, open the file itself with `O_EVTONLY` and attach a second `DispatchSourceFileSystemObject` on that fd watching `.write, .extend, .attrib` on the same `watchQueue`, and check `pathIsReady()` from its handler. Also handle the case where the file already exists and is empty at the time of the initial call (attach the file source immediately). Keep the C11-209 invariants exactly: every fd is owned by its source and closed from the cancel handler only, `finishOnce` is the single terminal path, everything that mutates shared state runs on `watchQueue`, and the `v2AwaitCallback` deadline-unwind path cancels every live source. Do not reintroduce any `.main` queue usage in this path and do not widen the timeout cap. If you find a simpler correct approach (for example, a bounded low-frequency size poll on `watchQueue` as a fallback after the first directory event), that is acceptable if it cannot spin, but the file-level source is preferred. ## Tests Where a `c11LogicTests` seam is reachable, add one; if the handler is too entangled with `TerminalController` for a unit test, say so plainly rather than writing a fake test. A shell-level validation script (write a file empty, then append bytes 2 s later, and assert `c11 browser download wait --path

` returns early) belongs in the PR description as a repro even if it cannot run in CI. Do not run `xcodebuild` locally on this machine (one build per machine rule); CI is the gate. ## Validation Push, open the PR, watch `gh pr checks`, iterate until green.
data.title: browser download wait --path misses files created empty and written in place

data.body:
Plan (delegator, worktree agent-a60a6719f594a3d01, branch c11-222-download-wait-inplace):

1. Extract the watch logic out of v2BrowserDownloadWait into a new testable unit, Sources/SocketHandlers/DownloadPathWatcher.swift: a small class taking (path, queue) and a completion, with no TerminalController dependency.
2. Watcher behaviour: a directory source on the parent (O_EVTONLY, same mask as today) PLUS, whenever the target exists but is not yet ready, a second source on the file's own O_EVTONLY fd watching .write/.extend/.attrib/.delete/.rename on the same serial queue. The file source is attached from the initial on-queue evaluation too, so 'already exists and empty at call time' is covered. On delete/rename of the watched inode the file source is cancelled and rebound so a replaced file is still tracked.
3. C11-209 invariants preserved verbatim: every fd is owned by its source and closed only from that source's cancel handler; a single terminate() is the one terminal path (guarded by a 'finished' flag); every mutation runs on the private serial queue (single writer); teardown() after the v2AwaitCallback deadline unwind cancels BOTH sources and is idempotent. No .main queue anywhere in this path, no change to the timeout clamp.
4. Tests in c11LogicTests (DownloadPathWatcherTests.swift, real temp files): atomic rename into place resolves; create-empty-then-append-in-place resolves; already-present-empty-then-filled resolves; never-filled times out and every opened fd is closed. New files wired by hand into project.pbxproj (no PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup in this project), verified with plutil -lint.
5. No local xcodebuild (one-build-per-machine rule). CI is the gate; shell repro for the in-place case goes in the PR description.

Done: PR https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/437 (branch c11-222-download-wait-inplace), all CI checks green (build incl. the logic-test gate, compat-tests, build-ghosttykit, remote-daemon-tests, web-typecheck, workflow-guard-tests, drawbridge). Not merged; orchestrator's call.

What changed:
- New Sources/SocketHandlers/DownloadPathWatcher.swift. Takes (path, serial queue) and a completion; no TerminalController dependency. Keeps the parent-directory source and, whenever the target exists but is not yet ready, attaches a second DispatchSourceFileSystemObject on the file's own O_EVTONLY fd (.write/.extend/.attrib/.delete/.rename) on the same queue. That attach also runs in the initial on-queue evaluation, so an already-present empty file is covered. On delete/rename of the watched inode the file source is cancelled and rebound so a replaced target is still followed.
- v2BrowserDownloadWait now just builds the watcher, hands v2AwaitCallback its start(), and calls watcher.teardown() unconditionally after the await returns. Early-return readiness check now goes through DownloadPathWatcher.isPathReady.

C11-209 invariants: every fd is owned by its source and closed only from that source's cancel handler (the handlers close without needing self, so a dealloc cannot strand one); terminate(delivering:) is the single terminal path behind a finished flag, with nil meaning 'tear down, deliver nothing'; every mutation runs on the private serial queue with dispatchPrecondition assertions; teardown is idempotent and cancels both sources plus the deadline item. No DispatchQueue.main in the path, timeout clamp untouched, no dlog.

Tests: c11Tests/DownloadPathWatcherTests.swift in the c11LogicTests target, real temp files. Six cases (rename-into-place, create-empty-then-append, already-present-empty-then-filled, never-filled timeout with full fd accounting, teardown-before-resolution, isPathReady). All six ran and passed in CI in 1.2s total.

No xcodebuild was run locally. Instead both new files were type-checked with swiftc -typecheck, and the scenarios were run through a throwaway swiftc harness linking the real watcher: the fixed watcher resolves the in-place case in 0.22s, while a baseline build with the file source disabled (the pre-fix behaviour) fails exactly those two cases. The shell-level repro is in the PR description; it needs a live c11 with a browser surface, so it is not in CI.

PASS. PR #437 squash-merged; CI fully green on first push including the logic-test gate (6 DownloadPathWatcherTests against real temp files). Orchestrator reviewed: file-level DispatchSource attached whenever the target exists but is empty, covering create-empty-then-write and already-present-empty; delete/rename rebinds; every fd closed only from its source's cancel handler; single terminal path; all state on the private serial queue; no main-queue usage; synchronous finish is safe because v2AwaitCallback checks resolved immediately after start returns. Shell repro recorded in the PR description.
